question: In an office, how can I let the office network reach certain devices while stopping those devices from reaching back into the office network?
answer: Put the devices on the outside interface of a firewall; the office network can reach them but they cannot reach the office network.
support: place the things you don't want to get to your office network on the outside interface of the firewall

question: Once a TCP handshake has completed, can an attacker keep using that session after changing the source IP of their packets?
answer: No. A session is defined by source IP, source port, destination IP and destination port; changing the source IP makes it an out-of-state packet that is dropped or rejected.
support: When you change any one of those four parameters, like the source IP, the new packet is no longer a part of that TCP session

question: With nginx and PHP-FPM on 127.0.0.1:9000, what SCRIPT_FILENAME setting inside location / sends every request to a single index.php?
answer: fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root/index.php; together with include /etc/nginx/fastcgi_params and fastcgi_pass 127.0.0.1:9000.

question: Why is it a bad idea to design a fluent query-builder API so that its method chains read like full English sentences?
answer: English is ambiguous and needs context, users will write constructions you did not cover, and covering all of English is impossible; restricting to a subset just gives you SQL.
support: either you restrict yourself to a subset of English: that gives you SQL

question: How does the Linux kernel decide whether a partition name gets a separator letter, like mmcblk0p1 versus sda1, so I can predict it from the device name?
answer: If the last character of the disk name is a digit, the kernel inserts 'p' before the partition number (disk_name function in partition-generic.c).
support: If device name ends with digit then kernel adds 'p' symbol to separate partition number from device name.

question: In Postgres, how can I select rows where a comma-delimited text column contains any of several given strings?
answer: Convert with string_to_array(oe, ',') and use the overlaps operator &&, e.g. where string_to_array(oe, ',') && array['F3DH19860AA', 'F4DHAA'].

question: Why is keeping an auth token in browser local storage weaker against XSS than keeping a session cookie?
answer: Local storage is readable by same-domain JavaScript and has no equivalent of the HttpOnly flag, which session cookies can use to hide from malicious scripts.
support: there is no option to secure session identifier from XSS attacks unlike HTTPOnly security flag

question: On Linux, which command adds a second IP address to a single network interface, and what should you add so traffic uses it?
answer: ip addr add IFADDR dev STRING (address and device name); then specify routes that use that address with ip route.
support: the command is ip addr add IFADDR dev STRING

question: I aliased ls to lsc and lsc to 'ls -Flatr --color=always'. Running lsc says command not found. Why?
answer: lsc expands to ls, which expands back to lsc; bash will not expand lsc a second time, and no real lsc program exists.
support: bash refuses to expand it a second time

question: After moving to SQL Server 2012, my check IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#foo') > 0 before dropping a temp table stopped working. What changed and what is the fix?
answer: Temp tables now get a negative object_id in 2012, so test IF OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#foo') IS NOT NULL instead.
support: since #temp tables now get a negative object_id

question: Can I run a graphical app in Docker on a headless server by mounting the X11 libraries from a separate container through a volume?
answer: No: the program needs X11 libs and an X11 buffer (vnc/xvfb) itself; sharing libraries via a volume creates a hard dependency and likely crashes.
support: You can't run a program running on x11 without a x11 buffer somewhere, be it vnc, xvfb or whatever.

question: On a Cisco router with DMVPN and dual ISPs, how can I automatically shut down and bring back a tunnel interface when a tracked object changes state?
answer: Two EEM applets: one on 'event track 89 state down' runs 'shut' on the interface, the other on 'state up' runs 'no shut'.

question: To contain the impact of XSS from user-entered JavaScript, how should the main site and cookie scope be set up across subdomains?
answer: Serve the main site on www.site.com and make sure no cookie is scoped to *.site.com; Same Origin Policy then isolates subdomain DOM and cookies.
support: Just make sure your main site is www.site.com and no cookie is scoped to *.site.com

question: My self-made certificate with SANs works in Chrome but fails in openssl s_client and curl. What openssl.conf extension settings fixed it?
answer: A simpler config: v3_req with basicConstraints CA:FALSE, keyUsage nonRepudiation, digitalSignature, keyEncipherment, and subjectAltName = @alt_names; extra uncommented lines had conflicted.

question: What questions can I ask myself to decide whether an HTML table or CSS containers is the right choice for some content?
answer: Do rows or columns share a common attribute; would reordering them still make sense; would transposing rows and columns still make sense.
support: If I transposed the axes of the table (made rows into columns and vice-versa) would it still make sense?

question: In bash, why can't I store & in a variable to optionally background a command, and what works instead?
answer: Variable expansion happens after control operators are parsed; use a function that runs "$@" & when BCKGRND is "yes" and "$@" otherwise.
support: variable expansion happens after the command-line is parsed for control operators

question: How can I store dates before 1000 A.D. in MySQL while keeping them human readable?
answer: Use three numeric columns: year SMALLINT (negative for BC), month TINYINT, day TINYINT.
support: year SMALLINT # Store positive values for AD and negative for BC years.
